Two halves doing different jobs. A deterministic collector queries venue adapters and writes an evidence file in which a record cannot exist without a transaction hash, a URL or a document reference, because the schema will not represent one. The model writes the narrative from that file, and a gate checker reads the document and the evidence together before either ships.

Includes nine synthetic borrower fixtures covering a clean record, a cured delinquency, a default, a liquidation the collateral covered and one that left bad debt behind; a committed example dossier the tests regenerate and compare; a guide to closing a coverage gap that assumes no knowledge of Wildcat; 234 tests, none touching the network; and an audit log covering seventeen rounds including the fixes that were wrong the first time.

Gate 3 does the work. It rebuilds, from the evidence alone, every number and hash a truthful dossier could carry, using the same formatting helpers the renderer uses, then fails the document on any figure that is not in that set. An invented transaction hash, an amount rounded in the retelling, a market that was never there: each fails the run rather than shipping in it.

The ledger is a read-modify-write: an entry takes the previous entry's hash as its parent. Two hexctl processes interleaving there produce two entries claiming the same parent, and verify reports a broken chain afterwards. Nothing prevented that beforehand.
Only writers are locked. status, next and verify still answer while a run is held, so an agent that has just been refused can find out why rather than being locked out of the explanation too.

An O_EXCL create is the whole mechanism. Exactly one process wins, there is no dependency and nothing to configure. The refusal names the pid, the command it is running and when it started, and says what to do about it, because the case that produces it is two agents pointed at one directory and the fix is a worktree rather than a retry.
